) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Convert HTML into a PDF document.

    HTML is printed by a headless browser by default (``render_engine='auto'``),
    so JavaScript, modern CSS and background graphics are preserved. Pass
    ``slides=True`` (or use :func:`html_slides_to_pdf`) for slide decks.

    Args:
        source_path: Project HTML file to convert.
        content: Inline HTML content to convert.
        output_path: Project path for the PDF. Defaults to the source name.
        title: Optional document title metadata.
        pdf_engine: Preferred pandoc PDF engine (used when pandoc renders).
        **kwargs: Browser rendering options (``render_engine``, ``url``,
            ``slides``, ``page_size``, ``landscape``, ``media``,
            ``print_background``, ``margin``, ``page_break_selector``,
            ``wait_for_selector``, ``wait_timeout_ms``, ``script``).

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Confirmation with the generated PDF path.

    Example:
        >>> html_to_pdf(source_path="docs/page.html", output_path="docs/page.pdf")
        >>> html_to_pdf(source_path="docs/page.html", page_size="A4")
    """
    return doc_converter(
        target_format="pdf",
        source_path=source_path,
        content=content,
        output_path=output_path,
        source_format="html",
        title=title,
        pdf_engine=pdf_engine,
        **kwargs
    )


def html_slides_to_pdf(
    source_path: Optional[str] = None,
    content: Optional[str] = None,
    url: Optional[str] = None,
    output_path: Optional[str] = None,
    slides: bool = True,
    **kwargs
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Convert rich HTML slides into a PDF with the headless browser renderer.

    Applies the slide preset (1920x1080 landscape pages, screen media,
    background graphics, zero margins) and prints with Chromium so Reveal.js,
    Marp and custom CSS decks keep their layout, fonts and colors.

    Args:
        source_path: Project HTML deck to convert.
        content: Inline HTML deck to convert.
        url: Deck URL served locally (``http://localhost:...``) or a file URI.
        output_path: Project path for the PDF. Defaults to the source name.
        slides: Slide preset flag (True by default; override individual page
            options through ``**kwargs``).
        **kwargs: Any other :func:`doc_converter` option, e.g.
            ``page_break_selector``, ``wait_for_selector``, ``script``,
            ``media``, ``page_size``, ``landscape``, ``print_background``,
            ``margin``, ``wait_timeout_ms``.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Confirmation with the generated PDF path and renderer.

    Example:
        >>> html_slides_to_pdf(
        ...     source_path="slides/deck.html",
        ...     page_break_selector=".reveal .slides > section",
        ...     wait_for_selector=".reveal .slides section.present",
        ... )
    """
    return doc_converter(
        target_format="pdf",
        source_path=source_path,
        content=content,
        url=url,
        output_path=output_path,
        source_format="html",
        render_engine=kwargs.pop("render_engine", "auto"),
        slides=slides,
        **kwargs
    )

"""
SmolAgent: a small, async-only OpenAI chat agent.

Compared to the removed :class:`codx.junior.ai.openai_ai.OpenAI_AI`, this
implementation:
    * exposes a single async ``chat()`` method (no sync variant),
    * uses an **iterative** tool loop instead of recursion,
    * delegates loop protection to :class:`LoopGuard`,
    * delegates logging, event emission and cancellation to
      :class:`engine.agent_runtime.AgentRunContext`,
    * keeps streaming, callbacks, cancellation and analytics.
    * caches tool results per conversation to avoid re-execution.
    * returns a typed :class:`AgentRunResult` (no untyped ``additional_kwargs``).

Tool events (``TOOL_START`` / ``TOOL_END`` / ``TOOL_ERROR`` / ``TOOL_LOGS``) carry the
``tool_call_id``, the parsed JSON request args and a truncated result preview
so listeners (e.g. the ChatEventBridge) can surface tool executions as chat
messages in real time. ``TOOL_END`` additionally carries the dual-response tool's
user-facing ``output`` (see Message Structure below). Tool logs are emitted for
forensic audit trail.

Loop-Limit Handling
When :class:`LoopGuard` stops the run (max rounds, max tool calls or stuck
loop), the run is **not** aborted. Instead the tool-usage value is summarised
by the project's knowledge/RAG model and appended to the assistant answer, so
the findings survive in the persisted message and the next iteration can
continue without re-running the same tools. The summary request is
best-effort, does not count towards the loop limits, and its token usage is
recorded separately with the ``tool-analysis`` tag.

Cost-Limit Handling
Every round (iteration) computes its cost in cxjcoins from the provider usage
and the model price settings, accumulates it into the chat total and reports it
on the returned :class:`AgentRunResult` (``result.cost``). Tools that report
their own cost through :attr:`ToolResponse.cost` are summed into both the
per-run total and the chat total. The chat total is seeded from ``Chat.cost``
(the accumulated, deletion-safe value maintained by ChatManager) so the budget
applies to the whole chat and is not reset when messages are deleted. When the
chat reaches its estimated cost (``Chat.estimation_cost``), the run stops
gracefully — before executing further tools — to keep the chat within budget.

Message Structure
A single final assistant message is always produced. Its ``content`` holds only
the model's own text: reasoning emitted between tool rounds plus the final
answer. Tool output is NO LONGER merged into the message content. For
dual-response tools, ``ToolResponse.user_response`` is emitted on the ``TOOL_END``
event and attached to the response message as a collapsible property
(``ToolEvent.output``), so the client decides how to render it (collapsed or
hidden) and the chat stays clean.

Vision API Support
Binary files (PDFs, images) are passed as vision content when models support it.
The content is merged into the final user message to enable vision-capable models
to process images and documents alongside text.

Error Visibility
Every AI provider interaction (the completion request, the streaming of its
response and the tool-usage summary request) is guarded so failures are logged
VERBATIM: phase, model, provider, endpoint, whether an API key is configured,
message/tool counts, request/chat/run identifiers, HTTP status, provider
``code``/``param``/``request_id``, provider request-id header, response body
(truncated) and the chained root cause (``httpx.ConnectError``, DNS, TLS,
timeout, proxy, ...) — always followed by a full traceback. A short Markdown
notice with the same details is also streamed to the client, because previously
a failed connection surfaced as nothing more than the provider's generic
``"Connection error."`` string in both the logs and the chat.

- The converter (`doc_converter`) only decides *what* to render and calls the browser module; it must not import `playwright` at all.

## 2. Information Gathering

Current state on disk (verified):

- `codx/junior/browser/browser.py`: `Browser` (session CDP automation) with a **lazy** `from playwright.async_api import async_playwright` inside `connect()`. `execute_script`/`get_text` pass raw strings to `page.evaluate` although the tools document `return ...`.
- `codx/junior/browser/browser_manager.py` → `connect_browser()` builds `Browser(session, docker_manager)`; `browser/__init__.py` re-exports `Browser`/`BrowserManager`/`BrowserSession`.
- `codx/junior/browser/docker_firefox_manager.py` imports only stdlib + `browser.model` → importing `codx.junior.browser.browser` from the tools package is safe and cannot create an import cycle.
- `codx/junior/tools/doc_converter_tools.py` (current) is **pandoc-only**: `PANDOC_READERS`, `_convert_to_pdf`, `_convert_to_docx`, `_html_to_markdown`, `_build_output_path`, `_resource_path`, project path validation via `path_to_absolute_project_path`, `ToolResponse` dual response.
- `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py` already registers `doc_converter` (`DOC_CONVERTER_TOOL_JSON`, `project_settings=True, dual_response=True, scope="chat"`) → **registry needs no change**.
- `pyproject.toml` does not declare `playwright` although `browser.py` imports it.

## 3. Change Proposal & Refinement

1. **`browser.py` becomes the single Playwright owner.** New shared section before `Browser`:
   - `BrowserUnavailableError`, `playwright_available()`, `run_coroutine_sync()` (own loop, or a thread when a loop is already running — the agent calls sync tools inline), `normalize_script()`.

def playwright_available() -> bool:
    """
    Return True when the playwright package can be imported.

    The check is lazy and never raises: the Chromium binary itself is verified
    on launch, so callers can fall back to another renderer when it is missing.

    Returns:
        bool: True when playwright is importable.

    Example:
        >>> playwright_available()
        True
    """
    try:
        import playwright  # noqa: F401  (optional dependency, checked lazily)
        return True
    except Exception as ex:  # ImportError or a broken installation
        logger.debug("playwright is not available: %s", ex)

def run_coroutine_sync(coro_factory: Callable[[], Any]) -> Any:
    """
    Run a coroutine factory to completion from synchronous code.

    Playwright's async API must own its event loop. When this is called from a
    context that already has a running loop (the agent executes synchronous
    tools inline) the coroutine runs in a dedicated thread with a fresh loop.

    Args:
        coro_factory: Callable returning a **new** coroutine (it is invoked
            inside the destination loop, so pass a factory, not a coroutine).

    Returns:
        Any: The coroutine's return value.

    Example:
        >>> run_coroutine_sync(lambda: render_page("file:///tmp/a.html"))
    """
    try:
        asyncio.get_running_loop()
    except RuntimeError:
        # No loop running: safe to own the thread's loop
        return asyncio.run(coro_factory())

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as executor:
        return executor.submit(lambda: asyncio.run(coro_factory())).result()

    string starts with ``function``/``(``). Statements are wrapped into an arrow

    Args:

    Returns:
        Optional[str]: The expression/function to evaluate, or None when empty.

    Example:
        >>> normalize_script("return document.title")
        '() => { return document.title }'
        >>> normalize_script("() => Reveal.slide(0)")
        '() => Reveal.slide(0)'
    """
    stripped = (script or "").strip()
    if not stripped:
        return None
    if stripped.startswith("return "):
        return f"() => {{ {stripped} }}"
    # Arrow functions and function declarations are passed through untouched
    if stripped.startswith(("(", "function", "async", "()")):
        return stripped
    if "\n" in stripped or ";" in stripped:
        return f"() => {{ {stripped} }}"
    return stripped


def page_break_css(selector: str) -> str:
    """
    Build the print stylesheet that starts a new page per matched element.

    Each selector is handled separately so comma separated selector lists keep
    working, and the last match never emits a trailing blank page.

    Args:
        selector: CSS selector whose matches each start a new PDF page.

    Returns:
        str: CSS to inject into the page ("" when the selector is empty).

    Example:
        >>> page_break_css("section")
        '@media print {\\n  section { break-after: page; ... }\\n}'
    """
    parts = [part.strip() for part in (selector or "").split(",") if part.strip()]
    if not parts:
        return ""

    rules = [
        f"  {part} {{ break-after: page; page-break-after: always; }}"
        for part in parts
    ]
    rules += [
        f"  {part}:last-of-type {{ break-after: auto; page-break-after: auto; }}"
        for part in parts
    ]
    return "@media print {\n" + "\n".join(rules) + "\n}\n"


def parse_page_size(page_size: Optional[str]) -> Dict[str, str]:
    """
    Convert a page size argument into playwright ``page.pdf`` options.

    Args:
        page_size: Paper format ('A4', 'Letter', ...) or explicit dimensions
            ('1920x1080', '13.33in x 7.5in').

    Returns:
        Dict[str, str]: Empty dict for the browser default, otherwise
        ``format`` or ``width``/``height``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When the size cannot be parsed.

    Example:
        >>> parse_page_size("1920x1080")
        {'width': '1920px', 'height': '1080px'}
        >>> parse_page_size("A4")
        {'format': 'A4'}
    """
    size = (page_size or "").strip()
    if not size:
        return {}

    for page_format in PDF_PAGE_FORMATS:
        if size.lower() == page_format.lower():
            return {"format": page_format}

    lowered = size.lower()
    if "x" in lowered:
        width, _, height = lowered.partition("x")
        width, height = width.strip(), height.strip()
        if width and height:
            # Bare numbers are CSS pixels, units are kept as provided
            if width.replace(".", "", 1).isdigit() and height.replace(".", "", 1).isdigit():
                return {"width": f"{width}px", "height": f"{height}px"}
            return {"width": width, "height": height}

    raise ValueError(
        f"page_size '{page_size}' is not supported. Use a paper format "
        f"({', '.join(PDF_PAGE_FORMATS)}) or dimensions like '1920x1080' "
        "or '13.33in x 7.5in'"
    )


def parse_margin(margin: Optional[str]) -> Optional[Dict[str, str]]:
    """
    Convert a margin argument into playwright ``page.pdf`` margin options.

    Args:
        margin: Single CSS length applied to every side, or four comma
            separated values (top,right,bottom,left).

    Returns:
        Optional[Dict[str, str]]: Margins per side, or None when not requested.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When the number of values is not 1 or 4.

    Example:
        >>> parse_margin("1cm")
        {'top': '1cm', 'right': '1cm', 'bottom': '1cm', 'left': '1cm'}
    """
    value = (margin or "").strip()
    if not value:
        return None

    parts = [part.strip() for part in value.split(",") if part.strip()]
    sides = ("top", "right", "bottom", "left")
    if len(parts) == 1:
        return {side: parts[0] for side in sides}
    if len(parts) == 4:
        return dict(zip(sides, parts))

    raise ValueError(
        "margin must be a single CSS length ('0', '1cm') or four comma separated "
        "values: top,right,bottom,left"
    )


def pdf_options(
    page_size: Optional[str] = None,
    landscape: Optional[bool] = None,
    print_background: Optional[bool] = None,
    margin: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Build the playwright ``page.pdf`` options for the requested page layout.

    Args:
        page_size: Paper format or explicit dimensions.
        landscape: Print landscape (None keeps the browser default).
        print_background: Print CSS backgrounds (default True: rich documents
            and slides need it).
        margin: Page margins.

    Returns:
        Dict[str, Any]: Keyword arguments accepted by ``page.pdf``.

    Example:
        >>> pdf_options(page_size="1920x1080", landscape=True)
        {'print_background': True, 'landscape': True, 'width': '1920px', 'height': '1080px'}
    """
    options: Dict[str, Any] = {
        # Backgrounds carry most of the visual information of a rich document
        "print_background": True if print_background is None else bool(print_background),
    }
    if landscape is not None:
        options["landscape"] = bool(landscape)

    options.update(parse_page_size(page_size))

    margins = parse_margin(margin)
    if margins:
        options["margin"] = margins

    return options


def to_browser_target(target: str) -> str:
    """
    Resolve what playwright must open: URLs are kept, paths become file URIs.

    Args:
        target: ``http(s)://``, ``file://`` or a local file path.

    Returns:
        str: A URL playwright can navigate to.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When the target is empty.

    Example:
        >>> to_browser_target("/project/slides/deck.html")
        'file:///project/slides/deck.html'
    """
    if not target:
        raise ValueError("a page URL or file path is required")

    lowered = target.lower()
    if lowered.startswith(("http://", "https://", "file://", "data:", "about:")):
        return target
    return Path(target).resolve().as_uri()


class Browser:
    """
    High-level browser automation interface using Playwright.

    Manages Playwright context lifecycle and provides methods
    for page interaction (navigate, execute JS, take screenshots, etc.).

    ``connect()`` attaches to the *existing* page of the remote browser when one
    is available, so consecutive tool calls act on the same shared page.
    """

    def __init__(self, session: BrowserSession, docker_manager: DockerFirefoxManager):
        """
        Initialize Browser.

        Args:
            session: BrowserSession with container info
            docker_manager: DockerFirefoxManager instance
        """
        self.session = session
        self.docker_manager = docker_manager
        self.playwright = None
        self.browser = None
        self.context = None
        self.page = None

    async def connect(self) -> None:
        """
        Connect to the remote browser via the DevTools Protocol.

        Reuses the first existing context/page when present so that the shared
        browser state (current URL, DOM) is preserved across calls.

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If connection fails
        """
        try:
            from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

            self.playwright = await async_playwright().start()

            debug_url = self.session.debug_url
            logger.info("Connecting to browser at: %s", debug_url)

            # Attach to the running browser
            self.browser = await self.playwright.chromium.connect_over_cdp(debug_url)

            # Reuse an existing context/page when available (shared browser)
            contexts = self.browser.contexts
            if contexts:
                self.context = contexts[0]
            else:
                self.context = await self.browser.new_context()

            pages = self.context.pages
            self.page = pages[0] if pages else await self.context.new_page()

            logger.info("Browser connected: session %s", _short_id(self.session.id))
            self.session.mark_active()

        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("Failed to connect to browser")
            self.session.status = "error"
            self.session.error = str(e)
            raise RuntimeError(f"Browser connection failed: {e}")

    async def navigate(self, url: str) -> str:
        """
        Navigate to a URL.

        Args:
            url: URL to navigate to

        Returns:
            Current page title

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If page not connected
        """
        if not self.page:
            raise RuntimeError("Browser not connected")

        try:
            logger.info("Navigating to: %s", url)
            await self.page.goto(url, wait_until=BROWSER_WAIT_UNTIL)
            title = await self.page.title()
            self.session.current_url = url
            self.session.mark_active()
            return title
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("Navigation failed")
            raise RuntimeError(f"Navigation to {url} failed: {e}")

    async def execute_script(self, script: str) -> any:
        """
        Execute JavaScript in the page context.

        Args:
            script: JavaScript code to execute (use ``return ...`` to return a value)

        Returns:
            Result of script execution

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If page not connected
        """
        if not self.page:
            raise RuntimeError("Browser not connected")

        expression = normalize_script(script)
        if not expression:
            return None

        try:
            result = await self.page.evaluate(expression)
            self.session.mark_active()
            return result
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("Script execution failed")
            raise RuntimeError(f"Script execution failed: {e}")

    async def get_screenshot(self) -> str:
        """
        Take a screenshot of the current page.

        Returns:
            Base64-encoded PNG image (data: URI)

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If page not connected
        """
        if not self.page:
            raise RuntimeError("Browser not connected")

        try:
            screenshot_bytes = await self.page.screenshot(full_page=True)
            b64 = base64.b64encode(screenshot_bytes).decode("utf-8")
            self.session.mark_active()
            return f"data:image/png;base64,{b64}"
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("Screenshot failed")
            raise RuntimeError(f"Screenshot failed: {e}")

    async def get_content(self) -> str:
        """
        Get the current page HTML content.

        Returns:
            HTML string

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If page not connected
        """
        if not self.page:
            raise RuntimeError("Browser not connected")

        try:
            content = await self.page.content()
            self.session.mark_active()
            return content
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("get_content failed")
            raise RuntimeError(f"get_content failed: {e}")

    async def get_text(self) -> str:
        """
        Get the visible text of the current page (``document.body.innerText``).

        Returns:
            Visible text

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If page not connected
        """
        if not self.page:
            raise RuntimeError("Browser not connected")

        try:
            text = await self.page.evaluate(
                normalize_script("return document.body ? document.body.innerText : ''")
            )
            self.session.mark_active()
            return text
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("get_text failed")
            raise RuntimeError(f"get_text failed: {e}")

    async def click(self, selector: str) -> None:
        """
        Click an element.

        Args:
            selector: CSS selector

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If page not connected or element not found
        """
        if not self.page:
            raise RuntimeError("Browser not connected")

        try:
            await self.page.click(selector)
            self.session.mark_active()
            logger.debug("Clicked: %s", selector)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("Click failed for selector: %s", selector)
            raise RuntimeError(f"Click on {selector} failed: {e}")

    async def fill(self, selector: str, text: str) -> None:
        """
        Fill a text input.

        Args:
            selector: CSS selector
            text: Text to fill

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If page not connected or element not found
        """
        if not self.page:
            raise RuntimeError("Browser not connected")

        try:
            await self.page.fill(selector, text)
            self.session.mark_active()
            logger.debug("Filled %s with text", selector)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("Fill failed for selector: %s", selector)
            raise RuntimeError(f"Fill on {selector} failed: {e}")

    async def wait_for_selector(self, selector: str, timeout: int = 5000) -> None:
        """
        Wait for element to appear.

        Args:
            selector: CSS selector
            timeout: Timeout in milliseconds

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If element doesn't appear
        """
        if not self.page:
            raise RuntimeError("Browser not connected")

        try:
            await self.page.wait_for_selector(selector, timeout=timeout)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("Wait for selector failed: %s", selector)
            raise RuntimeError(f"Timeout waiting for {selector}: {e}")

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """
        Detach from the remote browser (the container keeps running).

        Closes only the Playwright connection — the remote Firefox page/state
        survives so it can be reused by the next call.
        """
        try:
            if self.context and self.browser and self.browser.contexts:
                # Do NOT close the shared context; only stop the local driver.
                pass
            if self.playwright:
                await self.playwright.stop()
            logger.info("Browser disconnected: session %s", _short_id(self.session.id))
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("Error closing browser: %s", e)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Browser(session={_short_id(self.session.id)}, connected={self.page is not None})"


class PdfPrinter:
    """
    Prints a rendered page to PDF with a local headless Chromium.

    Unlike :class:`Browser`, which drives the shared Firefox container, this
    launches its own headless Chromium so printing is isolated from the user
    session and works without Docker. JavaScript, modern CSS (flexbox/grid),
    custom fonts and background images are printed as a browser shows them,
    keeping text and links as vectors (no screenshots).

    Args:
        pdf_options: Keyword arguments for ``page.pdf`` (see :func:`pdf_options`).
        media: CSS media to emulate before printing ('screen' or 'print').
        wait_for_selector: Selector to wait for before printing.
        wait_timeout_ms: Extra delay in milliseconds before printing, so
            animations and async rendering settle.
        script: JavaScript executed right before printing.
        page_break_selector: Selector whose matches each start a new page.
        prefer_css_page_size: Use the page ``@page`` CSS size when present.

    Example:
        >>> printer = PdfPrinter(pdf_options=pdf_options(page_size="1920x1080"),
        ...                      media="screen",
        ...                      page_break_selector=".reveal .slides > section")
        >>> printer.print_target("slides/deck.html", "/project/slides/deck.pdf")
        'playwright-chromium'
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        pdf_options: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
        media: Optional[str] = None,
        wait_for_selector: Optional[str] = None,
        wait_timeout_ms: int = 0,
        script: Optional[str] = None,
        page_break_selector: Optional[str] = None,
        prefer_css_page_size: bool = False,
    ):
        normalized_media = (media or "").strip().lower() or None
        if normalized_media and normalized_media not in BROWSER_MEDIA_TYPES:
            raise ValueError(
                f"media '{media}' is not supported. "
                f"Use one of: {', '.join(BROWSER_MEDIA_TYPES)}"
            )

        self.pdf_options = dict(pdf_options or {})
        self.media = normalized_media
        self.wait_for_selector = wait_for_selector
        self.wait_timeout_ms = int(wait_timeout_ms or 0)
        self.script = normalize_script(script)
        self.page_break_selector = page_break_selector
        self.prefer_css_page_size = bool(prefer_css_page_size)

    async def _navigate(self, page, url: str) -> None:
        """
        Open the page waiting for network idle, retrying with ``load``.

        Slide decks frequently poll or keep a websocket open, so ``networkidle``
        may never be reached; the retry keeps printing possible in that case.
        """
        try:
            await page.goto(url, wait_until=BROWSER_WAIT_UNTIL, timeout=BROWSER_TIMEOUT_MS)
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.warning(
                "networkidle wait failed (%s); retrying with '%s'",
                ex, BROWSER_WAIT_UNTIL_FALLBACK,
            )
            await page.goto(
                url, wait_until=BROWSER_WAIT_UNTIL_FALLBACK, timeout=BROWSER_TIMEOUT_MS
            )

    async def print_async(self, target: str, output_file: str) -> str:
        """
        Render a URL or a local file and print it to ``output_file``.

        Args:
            target: URL (``http(s)://``/``file://``) or local file path.
            output_file: Absolute path of the PDF to write.

        Returns:
            str: Renderer label (:data:`BROWSER_ENGINE_LABEL`).

        Raises:
            BrowserUnavailableError: When Chromium cannot be launched.
        """
        from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

        url = to_browser_target(target)

        async with async_playwright() as playwright:
            try:
                browser = await playwright.chromium.launch(
                    headless=True,
                    args=list(CHROMIUM_LAUNCH_ARGS),
                )
            except Exception as ex:
                # Browser binary or system dependencies missing
                raise BrowserUnavailableError(
                    f"the headless browser could not be started ({ex}); "
                    + PLAYWRIGHT_INSTALL_HINT
                ) from ex

            try:
                page = await browser.new_page()
                if self.media:
                    await page.emulate_media(media=self.media)

                await self._navigate(page, url)

                if self.wait_for_selector:
                    await page.wait_for_selector(
                        self.wait_for_selector, timeout=BROWSER_TIMEOUT_MS
                    )

                if self.script:
                    await page.evaluate(self.script)

                if self.wait_timeout_ms:
                    await page.wait_for_timeout(self.wait_timeout_ms)

                if self.page_break_selector:
                    await page.add_style_tag(
                        content=page_break_css(self.page_break_selector)
                    )

                await page.pdf(
                    path=output_file,
                    prefer_css_page_size=self.prefer_css_page_size,
                    **self.pdf_options,
                )
            finally:
                await browser.close()

        logger.info("PDF printed with %s: %s", BROWSER_ENGINE_LABEL, output_file)
        return BROWSER_ENGINE_LABEL

    def print_target(self, target: str, output_file: str) -> str:
        """
        Synchronous, event-loop safe wrapper around :meth:`print_async`.

        Args:
            target: URL or local file path to render.
            output_file: Absolute path of the PDF to write.

        Returns:
            str: Renderer label (:data:`BROWSER_ENGINE_LABEL`).

        Raises:
            BrowserUnavailableError: When playwright or Chromium is missing.
        """
        try:
            return run_coroutine_sync(lambda: self.print_async(target, output_file))
        except BrowserUnavailableError:
            raise
        except ImportError as ex:
            raise BrowserUnavailableError(
                "the playwright package is not installed; " + PLAYWRIGHT_INSTALL_HINT
            ) from ex
        except Exception as ex:
            message = str(ex)
            if any(hint in message for hint in _BROWSER_MISSING_HINTS):
                raise BrowserUnavailableError(
                    f"the headless browser is not available ({message}); "
                    + PLAYWRIGHT_INSTALL_HINT
                ) from ex
            raise

PDF_ENGINES = ("xelatex", "lualatex", "pdflatex", "weasyprint", "wkhtmltopdf", "typst")

DEFAULT_PDF_ENGINE = "xelatex"

# Rendering engines used for html -> pdf
RENDER_ENGINES = ("auto", "browser", "pandoc")
DEFAULT_RENDER_ENGINE = "auto"

# Maximum characters of converted markdown returned inline in the response
MAX_INLINE_MARKDOWN_CHARS = 20000

# Default output name when neither 'source_path' nor 'output_path' is given
DEFAULT_OUTPUT_NAME = "document"

class _BrowserRendererUnavailable(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the browser renderer used to print PDFs cannot be used."""


def _resolve_project_path(
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings, file_path: str
) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Resolve a relative or absolute path and ensure it stays inside the project.

    Args:
        settings: The project settings.
        file_path: Relative or absolute path to resolve.

    Returns:
        Optional[str]: Normalized absolute path, or None when it escapes the
        project root.

    Example:
        >>> _resolve_project_path(settings, "docs/guide.md")
        '/project/docs/guide.md'
    """
    if not file_path:
        return None

    abs_path = path_to_absolute_project_path(settings=settings, file_path=file_path)
    if not abs_path:
        return None

    abs_path = os.path.normpath(abs_path)
    project_root = os.path.normpath(settings.abs_project_path)
    if abs_path != project_root and not abs_path.startswith(project_root + os.sep):
        logger.warning("Path outside project root: %s", file_path)
        return None
    return abs_path


def _to_relative_path(settings: CODXJuniorSettings, abs_path: str) -> str:
    """
    Convert an absolute path into a project-relative path when possible.

    Args:
        settings: The project settings.
        abs_path: Absolute path to convert.

    Returns:
        str: Project-relative path (or the original path when outside).
    """
    if abs_path.startswith(settings.abs_project_path):
        return os.path.relpath(abs_path, settings.abs_project_path)
    return abs_path


def _detect_source_format(source_path: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Infer the source format from a file extension.

    Args:
        source_path: Project file path used as conversion source.

    Returns:
        Optional[str]: 'markdown', 'html', or None when it cannot be inferred.

    Example:
        >>> _detect_source_format("docs/guide.md")
        'markdown'
    """
    if not source_path:
        return None

    extension = os.path.splitext(source_path)[1].lower()
    for source_format, extensions in SOURCE_FORMAT_EXTENSIONS.items():
        if extension in extensions:
            return source_format
    return None


def _resolve_source_format(
    source_format: Optional[str], source_path: Optional[str]
) -> str:
    """
    Determine the source format from the argument or the file extension.

    Args:
        source_format: Explicit source format provided by the caller.
        source_path: Project file path used as conversion source.

    Returns:
        str: Resolved source format ('markdown' or 'html').

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the format is invalid or cannot be inferred.
    """
    if source_format:
        resolved = source_format.strip().lower()
        if resolved not in SOURCE_FORMATS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"source_format '{source_format}' is not supported. "
                f"Use one of: {', '.join(SOURCE_FORMATS)}"
            )
        return resolved

    detected = _detect_source_format(source_path=source_path)
    if detected:
        return detected

    raise ValueError(
        "source_format ('markdown' or 'html') is required when the source is inline "
        "'content' or when the file extension is not recognized"
    )


def _build_output_path(
    source_path: Optional[str], output_path: Optional[str], target_format: str
) -> str:
    """
    Build the project-relative output path for the converted document.

    Args:
        source_path: Source file path, used to derive the default name.
        output_path: Explicit output path provided by the caller.
        target_format: Conversion target format.

    Returns:
        str: Project-relative output path.

    Example:
        >>> _build_output_path("docs/guide.md", None, "pdf")
        'docs/guide.pdf'
        >>> _build_output_path(None, "exports/manual", "docx")
        'exports/manual.docx'
    """
    extension = OUTPUT_EXTENSIONS[target_format]

    if output_path:
        # Keep the caller path but ensure it carries the target extension
        if not os.path.splitext(output_path)[1]:
            return f"{output_path}{extension}"
        return output_path

    stem = DEFAULT_OUTPUT_NAME
    folder = ""
    if source_path:
        stem = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(source_path))[0] or DEFAULT_OUTPUT_NAME
        folder = os.path.dirname(source_path)

    file_name = f"{stem}{extension}"
    return os.path.join(folder, file_name) if folder else file_name


def _resource_path(settings: CODXJuniorSettings, source_abs_path: Optional[str]) -> str:
    """
    Build the pandoc ``--resource-path`` value to resolve relative resources.

    Relative images and links are looked up first next to the source file and
    then at the project root.

    Args:
        settings: The project settings.
        source_abs_path: Absolute path of the source file, if any.

    Returns:
        str: Colon separated list of resource folders.

    Example:
        >>> _resource_path(settings, "/project/docs/guide.md")
        '/project/docs:/project'
    """
    folders = [os.path.normpath(settings.abs_project_path)]
    if source_abs_path:
        folders.insert(0, os.path.dirname(source_abs_path))
    # Remove duplicates while keeping order
    return os.pathsep.join(dict.fromkeys(folders))


def _pdf_engine_candidates(pdf_engine: Optional[str]) -> list:
    """
    Build the ordered list of PDF engines to try.

    The requested engine is tried first, then the remaining known engines up to
    ``MAX_PDF_ENGINE_ATTEMPTS``. An empty engine means "let pandoc decide".

    Args:
        pdf_engine: Engine requested by the caller.

    Returns:
        list: Engine names to attempt in order.

    Example:
        >>> _pdf_engine_candidates("weasyprint")
        ['weasyprint', 'xelatex', 'lualatex']
    """
    requested = (pdf_engine or "").strip().lower()
    candidates = [requested]
    for engine in PDF_ENGINES:
        if len(candidates) >= MAX_PDF_ENGINE_ATTEMPTS:
            break
        if engine != requested:
            candidates.append(engine)
    return candidates


def _ensure_pandoc() -> str:
    """
    Verify that the pandoc binary is available.

    Returns:
        str: Installed pandoc version.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: When pandoc is not installed or not found in the PATH.
    """
    try:
        return pypandoc.get_pandoc_version()
    except OSError as ex:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "pandoc binary is not available. Install pandoc (e.g. 'apt-get install pandoc') "
            "and a PDF engine ('texlive-xetex' for the default xelatex engine) to enable "
            "PDF and DOCX conversions."
        ) from ex


def _html_to_markdown(html: str) -> str:
    """
    Convert HTML into markdown using BeautifulSoup and html2text.

    Scripts and styles are removed and tables, links and images are preserved,
    matching the behaviour of ``fetch_webpage``.

    Args:
        html: HTML source content.

    Returns:
        str: Markdown representation of the HTML content.

    Example:
        >>> _html_to_markdown("<h1>Title</h1><p>Text</p>")
        '# Title\\n\\nText'
    """
    soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser")

    # Remove non textual elements
    for tag in soup(["script", "style"]):
        tag.decompose()

    converter = html2text.HTML2Text()
    converter.body_width = 0  # No line wrapping
    converter.ignore_images = False
    converter.ignore_emphasis = False
    converter.ignore_links = False
    converter.ignore_tables = False

    return converter.handle(str(soup)).strip()


def _pandoc_extra_args(
    resource_path: str, title: Optional[str] = None
) -> list:
    """
    Build the common pandoc arguments for document conversions.

    Args:
        resource_path: Folders used to resolve relative resources.
        title: Optional document title metadata.

    Returns:
        list: pandoc extra arguments.
    """
    extra_args = ["--standalone"]
    if resource_path:
        extra_args += ["--resource-path", resource_path]
    if title:
        extra_args += ["--metadata", f"title={title}"]
    return extra_args


def _convert_to_docx(
    content: str,
    source_format: str,
    output_file: str,
    resource_path: str,
    title: Optional[str] = None,
) -> None:
    """
    Convert content into a DOCX file with pandoc.

    Args:
        content: Source content to convert.
        source_format: Source format ('markdown' or 'html').
        output_file: Absolute path of the DOCX file to write.
        resource_path: Folders used to resolve relative resources.
        title: Optional document title metadata.

    Raises:
        Exception: Propagated from pandoc when the conversion fails.
    """
    logger.debug("Converting %s to docx: %s", source_format, output_file)
    pypandoc.convert_text(
        content,
        to="docx",
        format=PANDOC_READERS[source_format],
        outputfile=output_file,
        extra_args=_pandoc_extra_args(resource_path=resource_path, title=title),
    )


def _convert_to_pdf(
    content: str,
    source_format: str,
    output_file: str,
    resource_path: str,
    pdf_engine: Optional[str] = DEFAULT_PDF_ENGINE,
    title: Optional[str] = None,
) -> str:
    """
    Convert content into a PDF file with pandoc, trying alternative engines.

    Args:
        content: Source content to convert.
        source_format: Source format ('markdown' or 'html').
        output_file: Absolute path of the PDF file to write.
        resource_path: Folders used to resolve relative resources.
        pdf_engine: Preferred PDF engine (empty string lets pandoc decide).
        title: Optional document title metadata.

    Returns:
        str: The engine that produced the PDF ("" for the pandoc default).

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: When every attempted engine fails.
    """
    base_args = _pandoc_extra_args(resource_path=resource_path, title=title)
    errors = []

    for engine in _pdf_engine_candidates(pdf_engine=pdf_engine):
        extra_args = list(base_args)
        if engine:
            extra_args.append(f"--pdf-engine={engine}")
        try:
            logger.debug(
                "Converting %s to pdf with engine '%s': %s",
                source_format, engine or "default", output_file
            )
            pypandoc.convert_text(
                content,
                to="pdf",
                format=PANDOC_READERS[source_format],
                outputfile=output_file,
                extra_args=extra_args,
            )
            return engine
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.warning(
                "PDF conversion failed with engine '%s': %s", engine or "default", ex
            )
            errors.append(f"{engine or 'default'}: {ex}")

    raise RuntimeError(
        "no PDF engine could render the document ("
        + "; ".join(errors)
        + "). Install one of: "
        + ", ".join(PDF_ENGINES)
    )


def _browser_renderer_available() -> bool:
    """
    Return True when the browser renderer can print PDFs.

    Only the playwright package is verified here; the Chromium binary is checked
    on launch, so ``render_engine='auto'`` can safely fall back to pandoc.

    Returns:
        bool: True when the browser renderer is usable.
    """
    try:
        return playwright_available()
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        logger.debug("browser renderer not available: %s", ex)
        return False


def _validate_print_options(page_size: Optional[str], margin: Optional[str]) -> None:
    """
    Validate PDF layout options early so bad arguments raise ``ValueError``.

    Args:
        page_size: Page size argument to validate.
        margin: Margin argument to validate.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When a page size or margin value is invalid.
    """
    parse_page_size(page_size)
    parse_margin(margin)


def _print_pdf_with_browser(target: str, output_file: str, **options) -> str:
    """
    Print a URL or project file to PDF through the Playwright manager.

    All browser handling (launch, media emulation, page breaks, ``page.pdf``)
    lives in :mod:`codx.junior.browser.browser`; this wrapper only normalizes the
    exception so callers never depend on Playwright types.

    Args:
        target: URL or absolute file path to render.
        output_file: Absolute path of the PDF to write.
        **options: Print options forwarded to ``browser.print_pdf`` (``slides``,
            ``page_size``, ``landscape``, ``print_background``, ``margin``,
            ``media``, ``wait_for_selector``, ``wait_timeout_ms``, ``script``,
            ``page_break_selector``).

    Returns:
        str: Renderer label that produced the PDF.

    Raises:
        _BrowserRendererUnavailable: When Playwright or Chromium is missing.
    """
    try:
        return print_pdf(target=target, output_file=output_file, **options)
    except BrowserUnavailableError as ex:
        raise _BrowserRendererUnavailable(str(ex)) from ex


def _cap_markdown(markdown: str) -> str:
    """
    Trim converted markdown so the tool response stays reasonably small.

    Args:
        markdown: Converted markdown content.

    Returns:
        str: The markdown, truncated with a note when it exceeds the limit.
    """
    if len(markdown) <= MAX_INLINE_MARKDOWN_CHARS:
        return markdown
    return (
        markdown[:MAX_INLINE_MARKDOWN_CHARS]
        + "\n... (truncated, read the output file for the full content)"
    )


def doc_converter(
    target_format: str,
    content: Optional[str] = None,
    source_path: Optional[str] = None,
    output_path: Optional[str] = None,
    source_format: Optional[str] = None,
    title: Optional[str] = None,
    pdf_engine: str = DEFAULT_PDF_ENGINE,
    render_engine: str = DEFAULT_RENDER_ENGINE,
    url: Optional[str] = None,
    slides: bool = False,
    page_size: Optional[str] = None,
    landscape: Optional[bool] = None,
    media: Optional[str] = None,
    print_background: Optional[bool] = None,
    margin: Optional[str] = None,
    page_break_selector: Optional[str] = None,
    wait_for_selector: Optional[str] = None,
    wait_timeout_ms: int = 0,
    script: Optional[str] = None,
    **kwargs
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Convert a document or content between formats and save it in the project.

    Supported conversions:

    - markdown -> pdf: rendered with pandoc and the selected PDF engine.
    - markdown -> docx: rendered with pandoc.
    - html -> markdown: rendered with BeautifulSoup + html2text, no external binary.
    - html -> pdf: printed by a headless Chromium (default) or pandoc.

    Rich HTML slides use the browser renderer: ``slides=True`` sets a 16:9
    landscape page with screen media, background graphics and no margins, and
    ``page_break_selector`` gives each slide its own PDF page.

    Args:
        target_format: Target format: 'pdf', 'docx' or 'markdown'.
        content: Inline source content (exclusive with ``source_path``/``url``).
        source_path: Project file used as source (exclusive with ``content``/``url``).
        output_path: Project path for the converted file. Defaults to the source
            name with the target extension.
        source_format: 'markdown' or 'html'. Inferred from ``source_path``.
        title: Optional document title metadata for pdf/docx outputs.
        pdf_engine: Preferred pandoc PDF engine, default 'xelatex'. Alternative
            engines are tried when it is unavailable or fails.
        render_engine: Renderer for html -> pdf: 'auto' (browser, pandoc
            fallback), 'browser' (force) or 'pandoc'.
        url: Page URL to render with the browser engine (html -> pdf only).
        slides: Slide deck preset (1920x1080, landscape, screen media,
            backgrounds, zero margins).
        page_size: Paper format ('A4', 'Letter') or '1920x1080' / '13.33in x 7.5in'.
        landscape: Print landscape (defaults to True with ``slides``).
        media: CSS media emulated before printing ('screen' or 'print').
        print_background: Print CSS backgrounds (default True).
        margin: Page margin, one CSS length or four comma separated values.
        page_break_selector: Selector whose matches each start a new PDF page.
        wait_for_selector: Selector to wait for before printing.
        wait_timeout_ms: Extra delay in milliseconds before printing.
        script: JavaScript executed right before printing.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Contains:
            - user_response: Confirmation with the output path, size and renderer.
            - llm_response: Conversion details plus the converted markdown when
              the target format is markdown.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the arguments are invalid or the conversion pair is not
            supported.

    Example:
        >>> doc_converter(target_format="pdf", source_path="docs/guide.md")
        # ToolResponse with 'docs/guide.pdf' written in the project

        >>> doc_converter(
        ...     target_format="pdf",
        ...     source_path="slides/deck.html",
        ...     slides=True,
        ...     page_break_selector=".reveal .slides > section",
        ...     wait_for_selector=".reveal .slides section.present",
        ... )
        # Rich slide deck printed page by page with headless Chromium

        >>> doc_converter(
        ...     target_format="markdown",
        ...     content="<h1>Hello</h1>",
        ...     source_format="html",
        ...     output_path="docs/hello.md"
        ... )
        # ToolResponse with '# Hello' included inline and saved to docs/hello.md
    """
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings = kwargs.get("settings", None)
    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    normalized_target = (target_format or "").strip().lower()
    if normalized_target not in TARGET_FORMATS:
        raise ValueError(
            f"target_format '{target_format}' is not supported. "
            f"Use one of: {', '.join(TARGET_FORMATS)}"
        )

    normalized_engine = (render_engine or DEFAULT_RENDER_ENGINE).strip().lower()
    if normalized_engine not in RENDER_ENGINES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"render_engine '{render_engine}' is not supported. "
            f"Use one of: {', '.join(RENDER_ENGINES)}"
        )

    if media and media.strip().lower() not in BROWSER_MEDIA_TYPES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"media '{media}' is not supported. Use one of: {', '.join(BROWSER_MEDIA_TYPES)}"
        )

    if normalized_target == "pdf" and (page_size or margin):
        _validate_print_options(page_size=page_size, margin=margin)

    if url:
        if content or source_path:
            raise ValueError("Use 'url', 'content' or 'source_path', not more than one")
        if normalized_target != "pdf":
            raise ValueError("url sources can only be converted to pdf")
        if normalized_engine == "pandoc":
            raise ValueError(
                "url sources can only be rendered with the browser engine; "
                "use render_engine='auto' or 'browser'"
            )
        # A URL always renders as a web page
        source_format = source_format or "html"
    elif not content and not source_path:
        raise ValueError(
            "Provide 'content' (inline source), 'source_path' (project file) or 'url'"
        )
    elif content and source_path:
        raise ValueError("Use 'content' or 'source_path', not both")

    resolved_source_format = _resolve_source_format(
        source_format=source_format, source_path=source_path
    )

    if (resolved_source_format, normalized_target) not in SUPPORTED_CONVERSIONS:

        source_format="markdown",
        title=title,
        pdf_engine=pdf_engine,

    )

    pdf_engine: str = DEFAULT_PDF_ENGINE,
    **kwargs
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Convert HTML into a PDF document.

    HTML is printed by a headless browser by default (``render_engine='auto'``),
    so JavaScript, modern CSS and background graphics are preserved. Pass
    ``slides=True`` (or use :func:`html_slides_to_pdf`) for slide decks.

    Args:
        source_path: Project HTML file to convert.
        content: Inline HTML content to convert.
        output_path: Project path for the PDF. Defaults to the source name.
        title: Optional document title metadata.

        **kwargs: Browser rendering options (``render_engine``, ``url``,
            ``slides``, ``page_size``, ``landscape``, ``media``,
            ``print_background``, ``margin``, ``page_break_selector``,
            ``wait_for_selector``, ``wait_timeout_ms``, ``script``).

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Confirmation with the generated PDF path.

    Example:
        >>> html_to_pdf(source_path="docs/page.html", output_path="docs/page.pdf")
        >>> html_to_pdf(source_path="docs/page.html", page_size="A4")
    """
    return doc_converter(
        target_format="pdf",
        source_path=source_path,
        content=content,
        output_path=output_path,
        source_format="html",
        title=title,
        pdf_engine=pdf_engine,
        **kwargs
    )


def html_slides_to_pdf(
    source_path: Optional[str] = None,
    content: Optional[str] = None,
    url: Optional[str] = None,
    output_path: Optional[str] = None,
    slides: bool = True,
    **kwargs
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Convert rich HTML slides into a PDF with the browser renderer.

    Applies the slide preset (1920x1080 landscape pages, screen media,
    background graphics, zero margins) and prints with headless Chromium so
    Reveal.js, Marp and custom CSS decks keep their layout, fonts and colors.

    Args:
        source_path: Project HTML deck to convert.
        content: Inline HTML deck to convert.
        url: Deck URL served locally (``http://localhost:...``) or a file URI.
        output_path: Project path for the PDF. Defaults to the source name.
        slides: Slide preset flag (True by default; override individual page
            options through ``**kwargs``).
        **kwargs: Any other :func:`doc_converter` option, e.g.
            ``page_break_selector``, ``wait_for_selector``, ``script``,
            ``media``, ``page_size``, ``landscape``, ``print_background``,
            ``margin``, ``wait_timeout_ms``.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Confirmation with the generated PDF path and renderer.

    Example:
        >>> html_slides_to_pdf(
        ...     source_path="slides/deck.html",
        ...     page_break_selector=".reveal .slides > section",
        ...     wait_for_selector=".reveal .slides section.present",
        ... )
    """
    return doc_converter(
        target_format="pdf",
        source_path=source_path,
        content=content,
        url=url,
        output_path=output_path,
        source_format="html",
        render_engine=kwargs.pop("render_engine", DEFAULT_RENDER_ENGINE),
        slides=slides,
        **kwargs
    )

Handles container creation, connection setup, and cleanup with Traefik routing.

-------------------
- ``stop_container(session, remove=True)``  : stop + remove (full teardown).
- ``stop_container(session, remove=False)`` : stop only — the container is kept
  so it can be started again with ``restart_container`` (state preserved).
- ``restart_container(session)``            : starts an existing (stopped)

    - Persistent profile volume for session state

class _BrowserRendererUnavailable(RuntimeError):

def _resolve_project_path(
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings, file_path: str
) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Resolve a relative or absolute path and ensure it stays inside the project.

    Args:
        settings: The project settings.
        file_path: Relative or absolute path to resolve.

    Returns:
        Optional[str]: Normalized absolute path, or None when it escapes the
        project root.

    Example:
        >>> _resolve_project_path(settings, "docs/guide.md")
        '/project/docs/guide.md'
    """
    if not file_path:
        return None

    abs_path = path_to_absolute_project_path(settings=settings, file_path=file_path)
    if not abs_path:
        return None

    abs_path = os.path.normpath(abs_path)
    project_root = os.path.normpath(settings.abs_project_path)
    if abs_path != project_root and not abs_path.startswith(project_root + os.sep):
        logger.warning("Path outside project root: %s", file_path)
        return None
    return abs_path


def _to_relative_path(settings: CODXJuniorSettings, abs_path: str) -> str:
    """
    Convert an absolute path into a project-relative path when possible.

    Args:
        settings: The project settings.
        abs_path: Absolute path to convert.

    Returns:
        str: Project-relative path (or the original path when outside).
    """
    if abs_path.startswith(settings.abs_project_path):
        return os.path.relpath(abs_path, settings.abs_project_path)
    return abs_path


def _detect_source_format(source_path: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Infer the source format from a file extension.

    Args:
        source_path: Project file path used as conversion source.

    Returns:
        Optional[str]: 'markdown', 'html', or None when it cannot be inferred.

    Example:
        >>> _detect_source_format("docs/guide.md")
        'markdown'
    """
    if not source_path:
        return None

    extension = os.path.splitext(source_path)[1].lower()
    for source_format, extensions in SOURCE_FORMAT_EXTENSIONS.items():
        if extension in extensions:
            return source_format
    return None


def _resolve_source_format(
    source_format: Optional[str], source_path: Optional[str]
) -> str:
    """
    Determine the source format from the argument or the file extension.

    Args:
        source_format: Explicit source format provided by the caller.
        source_path: Project file path used as conversion source.

    Returns:
        str: Resolved source format ('markdown' or 'html').

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the format is invalid or cannot be inferred.
    """
    if source_format:
        resolved = source_format.strip().lower()
        if resolved not in SOURCE_FORMATS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"source_format '{source_format}' is not supported. "
                f"Use one of: {', '.join(SOURCE_FORMATS)}"
            )
        return resolved

    detected = _detect_source_format(source_path=source_path)
    if detected:
        return detected

    raise ValueError(
        "source_format ('markdown' or 'html') is required when the source is inline "
        "'content' or when the file extension is not recognized"
    )


def _build_output_path(
    source_path: Optional[str], output_path: Optional[str], target_format: str
) -> str:
    """
    Build the project-relative output path for the converted document.

    Args:
        source_path: Source file path, used to derive the default name.
        output_path: Explicit output path provided by the caller.
        target_format: Conversion target format.

    Returns:
        str: Project-relative output path.

    Example:
        >>> _build_output_path("docs/guide.md", None, "pdf")
        'docs/guide.pdf'
        >>> _build_output_path(None, "exports/manual", "docx")
        'exports/manual.docx'
    """
    extension = OUTPUT_EXTENSIONS[target_format]

    if output_path:
        # Keep the caller path but ensure it carries the target extension
        if not os.path.splitext(output_path)[1]:
            return f"{output_path}{extension}"
        return output_path

    stem = DEFAULT_OUTPUT_NAME
    folder = ""
    if source_path:
        stem = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(source_path))[0] or DEFAULT_OUTPUT_NAME
        folder = os.path.dirname(source_path)

    file_name = f"{stem}{extension}"
    return os.path.join(folder, file_name) if folder else file_name


def _resource_path(settings: CODXJuniorSettings, source_abs_path: Optional[str]) -> str:
    """
    Build the pandoc ``--resource-path`` value to resolve relative resources.

    Relative images and links are looked up first next to the source file and
    then at the project root.

    Args:
        settings: The project settings.
        source_abs_path: Absolute path of the source file, if any.

    Returns:
        str: Colon separated list of resource folders.

    Example:
        >>> _resource_path(settings, "/project/docs/guide.md")
        '/project/docs:/project'
    """
    folders = [os.path.normpath(settings.abs_project_path)]
    if source_abs_path:
        folders.insert(0, os.path.dirname(source_abs_path))
    # Remove duplicates while keeping order
    return os.pathsep.join(dict.fromkeys(folders))


def _installed_pdf_engines() -> list:
    """
    Return the pandoc PDF engines whose executable is available in the PATH.

    Calling pandoc with an engine that is not installed only produces noise
    ("xelatex not found", missing metrics, missing rsvg-convert, ...), so
    unavailable engines are filtered out before conversion.

    Returns:
        list: Installed engine names, in :data:`PDF_ENGINES` order.

    Example:
        >>> _installed_pdf_engines()
        ['weasyprint']
    """
    return [engine for engine in PDF_ENGINES if shutil.which(engine)]


def _pdf_engine_candidates(
    pdf_engine: Optional[str],
    installed_engines: Optional[list] = None,
    preferred_engines: Optional[list] = None,
) -> list:
    """
    Build the ordered list of pandoc PDF engines to try.

    Only installed engines are returned. The requested engine comes first, then
    the engines preferred for the source format, then any other installed
    engine, up to ``MAX_PDF_ENGINE_ATTEMPTS``.

    Args:
        pdf_engine: Engine requested by the caller.
        installed_engines: Engines available on the system (all known engines
            when omitted).
        preferred_engines: Engines preferred for the source format.

    Returns:
        list: Engine names to attempt in order (empty when none is installed).

    Example:
        >>> _pdf_engine_candidates("weasyprint", ["weasyprint", "xelatex"])
        ['weasyprint', 'xelatex']
    """
    installed = list(PDF_ENGINES if installed_engines is None else installed_engines)
    if not installed:
        return []

    requested = (pdf_engine or "").strip().lower()
    preferred = list(preferred_engines or PDF_ENGINES)

    candidates = []
    if requested and requested in installed:
        candidates.append(requested)
    for engine in preferred + installed:
        if engine in installed and engine not in candidates:
            candidates.append(engine)
    return candidates[:MAX_PDF_ENGINE_ATTEMPTS]


def _ensure_pandoc() -> str:
    """
    Verify that the pandoc binary is available.

    Returns:
        str: Installed pandoc version.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: When pandoc is not installed or not found in the PATH.
    """
    try:
        return pypandoc.get_pandoc_version()
    except OSError as ex:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "pandoc binary is not available. Install pandoc (e.g. 'apt-get install pandoc') "
            "and a PDF engine ('texlive-xetex' for the default xelatex engine) to enable "
            "PDF and DOCX conversions."
        ) from ex


def _short_error(ex: Exception) -> str:
    """
    Collapse a converter error into a single, readable line.

    Pandoc and LaTeX errors are multi-line blobs; only the beginning carries the
    root cause ("xelatex not found", "Pandoc died with exitcode ...").

    Args:
        ex: Exception raised by the converter.

    Returns:
        str: Whitespace-normalized, length-capped error message.

    Example:
        >>> _short_error(RuntimeError("a\\n  b"))
        'a b'
    """
    text = " ".join(str(ex).split()) or ex.__class__.__name__
    if len(text) <= MAX_ENGINE_ERROR_CHARS:
        return text
    return text[:MAX_ENGINE_ERROR_CHARS] + "..."


def _html_to_markdown(html: str) -> str:
    """
    Convert HTML into markdown using BeautifulSoup and html2text.

    Scripts and styles are removed and tables, links and images are preserved,
    matching the behaviour of ``fetch_webpage``.

    Args:
        html: HTML source content.

    Returns:
        str: Markdown representation of the HTML content.

    Example:
        >>> _html_to_markdown("<h1>Title</h1><p>Text</p>")
        '# Title\\n\\nText'
    """
    soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser")

    # Remove non textual elements
    for tag in soup(["script", "style"]):
        tag.decompose()

    converter = html2text.HTML2Text()
    converter.body_width = 0  # No line wrapping
    converter.ignore_images = False
    converter.ignore_emphasis = False
    converter.ignore_links = False
    converter.ignore_tables = False

    return converter.handle(str(soup)).strip()

    extra_args = ["--standalone"]
    if resource_path:
        extra_args += ["--resource-path", resource_path]
    if title:
        extra_args += ["--metadata", f"title={title}"]

def _convert_to_docx(

) -> None:
    """
    Convert content into a DOCX file with pandoc.

def _convert_to_pdf(
    content: str,
    source_format: str,
    output_file: str,
    resource_path: str,
    pdf_engine: Optional[str] = DEFAULT_PDF_ENGINE,
    title: Optional[str] = None,
) -> str:
    """
    Convert content into a PDF file with pandoc, trying the installed engines.

    Only engines whose executable is present are attempted, and HTML sources
    prefer HTML capable engines (:data:`HTML_PDF_ENGINES`) because LaTeX cannot
    render web pages.

    Args:
        content: Source content to convert.
        source_format: Source format ('markdown' or 'html').
        output_file: Absolute path of the PDF file to write.
        resource_path: Folders used to resolve relative resources.
        pdf_engine: Preferred PDF engine (empty string lets pandoc decide).
        title: Optional document title metadata.

    Returns:
        str: The engine that produced the PDF ("" for the pandoc default).

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: When no engine is installed or every attempted engine
            fails.
    """
    base_args = _pandoc_extra_args(resource_path=resource_path, title=title)
    preferred = HTML_PDF_ENGINES if source_format == "html" else PDF_ENGINES
    candidates = _pdf_engine_candidates(
        pdf_engine=pdf_engine,
        installed_engines=_installed_pdf_engines(),
        preferred_engines=preferred,
    )

    if not candidates:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "no pandoc PDF engine is installed. Install one of: "
            + ", ".join(PDF_ENGINES)
            + " (e.g. 'pip install weasyprint' for html sources)"
        )

    errors = []

    for engine in candidates:
        extra_args = list(base_args)
        if engine:
            extra_args.append(f"--pdf-engine={engine}")
        try:
            logger.debug(
                "Converting %s to pdf with engine '%s': %s",
                source_format, engine or "default", output_file
            )
            pypandoc.convert_text(
                content,
                to="pdf",
                format=PANDOC_READERS[source_format],
                outputfile=output_file,
                extra_args=extra_args,
            )
            return engine
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.warning(
                "PDF conversion failed with engine '%s': %s", engine or "default", ex
            )
            errors.append(f"{engine or 'default'}: {_short_error(ex)}")

    raise RuntimeError(
        "no PDF engine could render the document (" + "; ".join(errors) + ")"
    )


def _browser_renderer_available() -> bool:
    """
    Return True when the browser renderer can print PDFs.

    Only the playwright package is verified here; the Chromium binary is checked
    on launch, so ``render_engine='auto'`` can safely fall back to pandoc.

    Returns:
        bool: True when the browser renderer is usable.

    try:
        return playwright_available()
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive

    """
    Print a URL or project file to PDF through the Playwright manager.

    All browser handling (launch, media emulation, page breaks, ``page.pdf``)
    lives in :mod:`codx.junior.browser.browser`; this wrapper only normalizes the
    exception so callers never depend on Playwright types.

    Args:
        target: URL or absolute file path to render.
        output_file: Absolute path of the PDF to write.
        **options: Print options forwarded to ``browser.print_pdf`` (``slides``,
